text:
The primary material of a candle is, scientifically speaking, a solidified sigh. It is wax, yes, but only if you believe in the tyranny of matter.

Gerald, who collects nothing because everything is too heavy to carry, hung ‘The Color of Wind’ on a wall that didn’t exist yet. The painting was a masterpiece of absence, framed in silence and lit by a candle made of pure logic, which burned out immediately because it couldn’t find a reason to stay lit.

At the auction, Gerald bid against himself using only his left elbow, winning the piece for the price of three forgotten Tuesdays. To celebrate, he hosted a grand dinner party for an audience of one: a chair. The table was empty, not because there was no food, but because the food was currently on strike, demanding better working conditions in the stomach. The guests ate nothing, which was delicious, because hunger has a crisp, metallic aftertaste that pairs well with the sound of a clock ticking backwards.
